title.narrative: Emergency Assistance for Rehabilitation and Reconstruction

description.narrative: In line with the Master Plan for Recovery and Reconstruction for Central Sulawesi (the Master Plan), the Emergency Assistance for Rehabilitation and Reconstruction (EARR) will support the Government of Indonesia in building back better critical infrastructure damaged by the devastating disasters in Central Sulawesi Province in September 2018, where a 7.4-magnitude earthquake triggered a near-field tsunami, landslides, and major liquefaction.

Status of Implementation Progress: Output 1: Human settlement infrastructure constructed, rehabilitated, and upgraded
"Reconstruction of Islamic University in Palu Subproject: The civil works contract was awarded in December 2020, for completion scheduled in December 2022. Construction is on-going with 83.12% physical progress as of Q3 2022.
"PASIGALA Source to Tap - Water Treatment and Distribution (WTD) Subproject: All civil works contracts awarded: (a) WTP Simoro: Awarded in April 2022 with 4.57% physical progress; (b) WTD Zone 1-2 and 3-4: Awarded in August 2022 with physical progress of 0.5% and 0.9%, respectively; (c) WTP Oloboju-Sidera: Awarded in August 2022 with 0.2% physical progress as of Q3 2022.
Output 2: Water resource infrastructure constructed, rehabilitated, and upgraded
"Gumbasa Irrigation System Subproject: All civil works for packages 1-3 awarded: (a) Package 1 (Weir and Groundsill): Awarded in August 2021 with 63.6% physical progress; (b) Package 2 (Main Canals BGKn. 7-24): Awarded in December 2021 with 27.8% physical progress; (c) Package 3 (Main Canals BGKn. 24-42): Awarded in December 2021 with 10.6% physical progress as of Q3 2022. Remaining civil works of package 4 is being prepared for contract signing in Q4 2022. The rehabilitation of tertiary canals in the upper part of the Gumbasa irrigation system (BGKn. 1-7), under community participation in procurement with the water user farmer's associations is ongoing.
"PASIGALA Source to Tap Subproject Raw Water Supply (RWS): (a) Paneki RWS (4.2 km new transmission system): Completed in December 2021; (b) PASIGALA 1 and 2 RWS (main RWS civil works 42 km existing and 39 km new transmission system): Awarded in October 2021 with 29.6% and 66.9% physical progress, respectively; and (c) Duyu RWS (1.5 km new transmission system): Awarded in May 2022 with 16% physical progress as of Q3 2022. Remaining civil works of Tondo RWS is being procured for award targeted in Q1 2023.
"Coastal Protection Subproject: Constructions completed for: (a) 7.2 km embankment protecting Palu City completed in December 2020; (b) boat mooring facilities and 0.75 km of Watusampu revetment completed in August 2022.
Output 3: Ports rehabilitated and reconstructed
"Reconstruction of Donggala Port (CW Port 1): The contractor was mobilized on 16 February 2022, expected completion by 11 June 2023. The actual construction progress as of 16 October 2022 is 44.64% against target of 56.54% (9.76% behind schedule).
"Reconstruction of Wani Port (CW Port 2): The contractor was mobilized on 25 April 2022, expected completion by 25 April 2023. The actual construction progress as of 16 October 2022 is 48.48% against target of 45.068% (3.13% ahead of schedule).
"Reconstruction of Pantoloan Port (CW Port 3): The contractor was mobilized on 4 October 2021, expected completion by 12 November 2022. The actual construction progress as of 16 October 2022 is 92.33% against the target of 95.80% (3,46% behind schedule).
"The Equipment Package for Cargo Handling for Donggala and Wani ports (EQ02): The package is being advertised for bid until 2 December 2022.
Output 4: Airport rehabilitated and reconstructed
"Reconstruction of Runway (CW Airport 1): The contractor was mobilized on 30 September 2021, expected completion by 24 March 2023. The actual construction progress is 41.40% against the target of 48.37% (2.97% behind schedule), as of 16 October 2022.
"Reconstruction of Terminal Building (CW Airport 2): The contractor was mobilized on 7 December 2021, expected completion by 31 March 2023. The actual construction progress is 44.25% against the target of 44.24% as of 16 October 2022.
